title: Gregory: A Man Named Gregory Who Works Here

beats.story: It takes sipping a full glass of water and staring at the tiles in the copy room for an unknown amount of time before I'm ready to return to the pods. I'm not quite on solid ground as I make my way to my desk. And when I do, my inbox waits with a formally toned email from Cliff, with attached instructions to close out our session from today and a note that he'll see me next week for the next one and promises that he'll continue to support my successful completion of the course. I type: Sounds good, thanks, hit send, close out, and stare forward, willing my emotions down. Willing myself to be a desk bot. I scan the other pods: Caitlin hasn't returned, but Armin is already back to dozing off in his seat like nothing happened. I notice that Rhonda's discreetly wiping her eyes with a tissue. We lock eyes only for a second before she averts my gaze and focuses on her screen.
beats.story_cn: 我足足灌下了一大杯水，对着打印间的瓷砖发了不知多久的呆，才勉强能重返隔间区。走回工位的步子仍有些虚浮。刚坐下，收件箱里就弹出Cliff那封措辞正式的邮件，附件里附着今天谈话的收尾指导，末了写着下周继续课程的约定，并承诺会支持我顺利完成课程。我敲下“收到，感谢”，点击发送，关掉页面，直视屏幕，强迫情绪下沉，逼自己变成一台工位机器人。扫视四周：Caitlin还没回来，但Armin已安然归座打瞌睡，仿佛什么都没发生。我瞥见Rhonda正用纸巾悄悄拭泪，我们目光刚触到一秒，她便躲开，凝神盯回屏幕。

beats.story: Gregory marches up to the cubicle block and says to me, "Caitlin never came back up, did she? Her reports are due." I shrug in the politest way possible, I think. Armin pipes in: "I saw her on her phone when I was coming back. Sounded like she was pissed at some wedding vendor or something. She was telling the guy to shut up." Gregory harumphs and stalks away toward the elevators, probably to find some intern to help him print something. Out of nowhere, Rhonda stands up, grabbing her quilted coat and embroidered purse. Armin looks up in surprise. "Hold up, you're not leaving, are you?" Rhonda looks at the floor, her chin wobbling.
beats.story_cn: Gregory大步走到隔间区，对我说：“Caitlin一直没回来吧？她的报告该交了。”我以自认为最得体的方式耸了耸肩。Armin插话：“我回来时看见她在打电话，听起来像在跟什么婚礼承办商发火，叫对方闭嘴。”Gregory哼了一声，转身朝电梯走去，大概又去找实习生帮忙打印什么。毫无预兆地，Rhonda站起身，抓起绗缝外套和刺绣手包。Armin惊讶地抬头：“等等，你不是要走吧？”Rhonda盯着地面，下巴微微发颤。

beats.story: "I'm needed somewhere. I have to go." "Is that so? I'm not sure you've cleared this time off with anyone." The corner of Armin's mouth pulls up into a self-satisfied smirk, and I get what he's doing, but I want to slap him because this is not the moment. "You haven't even sent me the copy I need for Greg's party yet. I'm heading to the print shop tonight." Rhonda rocks on her feet, her whole demeanor frail. "Right," she says slowly. "Okay, give me a few minutes." She starts to drop her bag again, and I catch moisture gathering in the corners of her eyes. "I can do it," I announce.
beats.story_cn: “我有事得走。”“是吗？我不确定你跟谁请过假了。”Armin嘴角勾起一抹自得的笑意，我明白他的算盘，却真想给他一巴掌——此刻绝不是时候。“Greg派对要的资料你还没发我呢，我今晚可要去印刷店。”Rhonda在原地晃了晃，整个人脆弱得像要散架。“好，”她慢吞吞地说，“给我几分钟。”她正要放下包，我瞥见她眼眶泛起水光。“我来做吧，”我开口道。

beats.story: The state of emergency in this place post - fire drill is something else. Armin looks toward me. "Jolene, if you're really doing the write-up about Gregory, I need it by four." "The what?" Oh god, what did I sign myself up for? Armin raises his eyebrows, a hint of amusement in his expression. "Rhonda wanted a written toast to sit on the tables for Gregory's anniversary party. Like, a quick summary of his career and awards, a short thing about his family life, I guess." This task is my personal nightmare, actually, but as I look at Rhonda's empty cube, I know of course I have to do it. A good way to not be okay is to spend a whole afternoon internet-stalking a man who every time you see his face, a part of you wants to curse your own existence because it means having to witness his. But the faster I finish, the quicker I can go home and drink the horrible new knowledge of Gregory away.
beats.story_cn: 火灾演习后这地方的紧急状态简直非同寻常。阿明看向我。“乔琳，如果你真要写格雷戈里的报告，四点前给我。”“什么报告？”天啊，我究竟揽下了什么差事？阿明扬起眉毛，眼里闪过一丝戏谑。“罗娜想要一份摆在格雷戈里周年庆宴席上的书面致辞。大概就概括下他的职业生涯与获奖情况，再简单提提家庭生活之类的。”这任务实为我的个人噩梦，但看着罗娜空荡的隔间，我明白自己别无选择。要体验生无可恋的滋味，莫过于花整个下午在互联网上追踪那个男人——每次瞥见他的脸，总有部分自我想诅咒自己的存在，因为那意味着不得不目睹他的存在。但越快完成，就能越早回家用劣酒浇灌关于格雷戈里的骇人新认知。

beats.story: The interesting slash depressing thing about working for a corporation that's been around for as long as Supershops has is that a lot of things that are obvious wastes of time and money have most certainly happened. In my deep dive of the company database, I've learned that between the years 2004 and 2013, the office had a "newspaper." It was literally a weekly periodical about the people here and the things they did. There's a notice about the formation of the office Coffee Club (decades old, who would have thought!), an article about the office-wide switch to Windows Vista, and a write-up of a Bring Your Child to Work Day, featuring an old picture of Rhonda with a young child hugging her waist, who the caption confirms is Carl. I stare at their beaming smiles for several seconds, every muscle in my body as heavy as lead. Gregory was featured in this newspaper three times. The first was on January 4, 2005, when Gregory launched a new motivational contest for the office employees. I could've used this, but Larry D. Goodwin won, and the picture is of Gregory handing him a laminated certificate.
beats.story_cn: 在超商店这样历史悠久的公司工作，有趣又憋屈的是，那些明显浪费时间和金钱的事，肯定都真实发生过。我在深挖公司数据库时发现，2004到2013年间，办公室竟有份“报纸”——字面意义上的周刊，记录这里的人和事。上面有办公室“咖啡俱乐部”成立的告示（几十年历史了，谁能想到！），有关于全员切换Windows Vista系统的报道，还有“带孩子上班日”的专题，配着朗达的老照片——一个小孩搂着她腰，图注证实那是卡尔。我盯着他们灿烂的笑容看了几秒，身体每块肌肉都沉得像铅。格雷戈里在这份报上出现过三次：第一次是2005年1月4日，他为员工发起了新激励竞赛。我本该学学这招，但拉里·D·古德温赢了，照片里格雷戈里正递给他塑封的证书。

beats.story: The second was on March 30, 2009, for winning a best tie contest. He's pictured holding up the neckwear in question to display the rubber duckie pattern -- such an asshole tie to buy. The third mention is on July 13, 2013, featuring him flipping pancakes for the annual company breakfast. It's an obvious photo-op moment: he's posing with a spatula, serving up a bullshit smile to someone holding a plate requesting actual food. The death glare from the person waiting in line behind them is a thing of beauty. It's nice to see like-minded people in the world. All three of these mentions have to do with team-building programs he launched that eventually died out. Obviously, I'm not really supposed to embarrass him in his toast, but the temptation bites.
beats.story_cn: 第二次是2009年3月30日，因赢得“最佳领带大赛”。照片里他举着那条小黄鸭图案的领带——真是傻逼才买的领带。第三次是2013年7月13日，专题报道他在年度公司早餐会上摊煎饼。摆拍痕迹明显：他举着铲子假笑，对端盘子索要真食物的人堆出虚伪笑脸。后面排队者的死亡凝视堪称艺术品——很高兴发现世上还有同道中人。三次上报都关于他发起最终夭折的团建活动。显然我本该在祝酒词里给他留面子，但这诱惑实在扎心。

beats.story: I do my best to pad the write-up with some vague sentences copied from the internet about things to say about great bosses, before moving on to the portion about his family life. I forgot his wife's name; she's that lady in the picture on his desk. But then it hits, the fastest way to find it: the Papa Bear email. I take some calming breaths before opening the message that knocks exactly six years off my life span every time I view it. Thankfully, Gregory has the email address listed in his contacts. I finish my write-up with: "During his free time, Gregory loves to BBQ, golf, and spend time with his loving wife, Sheila." I'll play the odds that either he is a BBQ golf guy or, if he isn't, he'll be flattered that people think he is. I shoot it off to Armin, and as I watch the email disappear from my screen, I wish that I could wipe this knowledge from my brain as easily.
beats.story_cn: 我尽力用网上摘抄的模糊句子填充这份吹捧文，才转向他家庭生活部分。我忘了他妻子名字——就是他桌摆照片里的女士。突然灵光一闪：最快捷径是那封“熊爸爸邮件”。每次打开这封每看一次减寿六年的邮件前，我都得深呼吸。谢天谢地，格雷戈里联系人里存着邮箱。我用这句话收尾：“闲暇时格雷戈里热爱烧烤、高尔夫，并与爱妻希拉共度时光。”赌他要么真是高尔夫烧烤爱好者，要么就算不是，也会为别人这么想而得意。邮件发给阿明的瞬间，我多么希望能像删除文件那样抹去这段记忆。

options.action: Take a calculated initiative to prevent minor misunderstandings from becoming compounded conflicts.
options.action_cn: 主动敏锐阻断小误会演变成连锁冲突。
options.fullOutcomeStory: Jolene kept her head clear and chose to prevent minor misunderstandings from becoming compounded conflicts. Her sharp wit and cautious maneuvering allowed her to navigate the tense moment without blowing her cover.
options.fullOutcomeStory_cn: 乔琳保持清醒，选择阻断小误会演变成连锁冲突。她机敏的才智与谨慎的周旋，让她在紧张时刻游刃有余，未露破绽。

options.action: Hesitate nervously and show signs of second-guessing yourself.
options.action_cn: 紧张犹豫，显露出自我怀疑的痕迹。
options.fullOutcomeStory: A momentary lapse in confidence caused everyone to stare in awkward silence. Caitlin seized the opportunity to throw a sarcastic smirk across the room.
options.fullOutcomeStory_cn: 自信陡然崩塌，引得众人面面相觑，空气里只剩僵持的寂静。凯特琳逮住这空当，隔着房间抛来一记阴冷的笑。

options.action: Overreact impulsively and blurt out something awkward.
options.action_cn: 冲动行事，脱口说出些不合时宜的话，平白将自己逼入窘境。
options.fullOutcomeStory: An impulsive burst of stress led to a bizarre remark that echoed through the quiet office. You immediately regretted speaking without filtering.
options.fullOutcomeStory_cn: 压力陡然爆发，竟迸出一句诡异言论，在寂静的办公室里嗡嗡回荡。你顿时懊悔不迭——方才怎就言未过脑？
